newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging mkt index starts week at 322.29 high.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging mkt index starts week at 322.29 high.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, opened the week at another new high of 322.29 on Monday after adding 0.5 percent on Friday.
Latin America edged up 1.4 percent day-on-day to 604.24, Asia was unchanged at 262.91 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.4 percent at 156.07.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 0.75 percent day-on-day at a new high of 175.14 at 1000 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, fell 0.05 percent to 126.38 by the start of trade on Monday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996. It hit its latest 1997 high last Thursday, at 126.44.
By region, Latin America was up 0.34 percent at 105.56, Asia fell 0.08 to 132.17 and East Europe was down 0.95 at 159.68.
